nodes.name: NiFe foam precleaning
nodes.procedure: Prior to the synthesis, NiFe foam with the size of 1 × 4 cm² was cleaned with HCl (1.0 M), ethanol, and ultrapure water successively.
nodes.source_text: Prior to the synthesis, NiFe foam with the size of 1 × 4 cm² was cleaned with HCl (1.0 M), ethanol, and ultrapure water successively.

nodes.name: HCl corrosion synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe foam was immersed into a semi-closed breaker containing 0.1 mM HCl solution. After 12 h corrosion at 90°C with a stirring rate of 250 rpm, the surface of NiFe foam was corroded completely. The corroded NiFe foam was collected and washed by ethanol and ultrapure water. The obtained foam (denoted as HCl-c-NiFe) was stored in ethanol at room temperature for further use.

nodes.characterization_summary: HCl-c-NiFe shows free-standing NiFe hydroxide nanosheets on the surface of NiFe foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows the scanning electron microscopic (SEM) image of HCl-c-NiFe. Obviously, HCl corrosion could induce the formation of fre-standing NiFe hydroxide nanosheets at the surface of NiFe foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: HCl-c-NiFe exhibits uniform structure of nanosheets (majority) and nanoribbons (minority) corresponding to NiFe hydroxides. HNO₃-c-NiFe and H₂SO₄-c-NiFe display irregular nanoribbon morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of HNO₃-c-NiFe (Fig. 1e) and H₂SO₄-c-NiFe (Fig. 1f) display irregular nanoribbon morphology, while HCl-c-NiFe (Fig. 1d) exhibits a uniform structure composed of nanosheets (majority) and nanoribbons (minority), corresponding to NiFe hydroxides with different structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: HCl-c-NiFe shows diffraction peaks at 11°, 23°, 46° for NiFe-LDH (003,006,018) and 14°, 27°, 36°, 46.5°, 60° for Fe(OH)₃. HNO₃-c-NiFe and H₂SO₄-c-NiFe show only Fe(OH)₃ phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks at 11°, 23° and 46° correspond to the (003), (006), and (018) lattice planes of NiFe-LDHs (JCPDF no. 51-0463), while the peaks at 14°, 27°, 36°, 46.5° and 60° can be assigned to the (020), (120), (031), (200), and (002) planes of lepidocrocite (Fe(OH)₃...

nodes.characterization_summary: HCl-c-NiFe exhibits higher surface Ni/Fe ratio than HNO₃-c-NiFe and H₂SO₄-c-NiFe, with decreased Ni(0) peaks (852.1 eV, 869.5 eV), decreased Fe(0) peaks (706.1 eV, 718.9 eV), and Fe³⁺ 2p₃/₂ peak negative shift to 711.8 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HCl-c-NiFe exhibits a much higher surface Ni/Fe ratio than that of HNO₃-c-NiFe and H₂SO₄-c-NiFe... After HCl corrosion, the intensity of Ni(0) peaks decrease obviously... the Fe³⁺ 2p₃/₂ peak for HCl-c-NiFe exhibits a negative shift from 712.2 eV to 711.8 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl values: HCl-c-NiFe 324 mF cm⁻², HNO₃-c-NiFe 176 mF cm⁻², H₂SO₄-c-NiFe 167 mF cm⁻², NiFe foam 26 mF cm⁻², indicating larger electrochemical surface area for HCl-c-NiFe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value for HCl-c-NiFe (324 mF cm⁻²) is much higher than HNO₃-c-NiFe (176 mF cm⁻²), H₂SO₄-c-NiFe (167 mF cm⁻²), and uncorroded NiFe (26 mF cm⁻²), indicating a larger electrochemical surface area for HCl-c-NiFe.

nodes.characterization_summary: HCl-c-NiFe shows β-Ni(OH)₂ peaks at 448 cm⁻¹, 532 cm⁻¹ transforming to NiOOH at 489 cm⁻¹, 557 cm⁻¹ and FeOOH at 655 cm⁻¹ at 1.4 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For HCl-c-NiFe, the initial Raman spectra at 1.0 V exhibits only two peaks at 448 cm⁻¹ and 532 cm⁻¹... When the potential is increased to 1.4 V, the two peaks present a positive shift to 489 cm⁻¹ and 557 cm⁻¹... a new peak appears at 655 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows OH peak at 531.6 eV and OOH peak at 529.1 eV for corroded catalysts. HCl-c-NiFe exhibits highest initial OOH ratio and highest OOH/OH ratio after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The wide O 1s peak located at 531.6 and 529.1 eV could be attributed to OH and OOH species... the HCl-c-NiFe exhibits the highest OOH/OH ratio than HNO₃-c-NiFe and H₂SO₄-c-NiFe.
